_note: The Matabele ant, Megaponera analis (M8 step 1c, docs/DESIGN.md 'Matabele colony, details'). Castes: the ergatoid (wingless) queen, and the workers, majors and minors on one continuous size spread (real Megaponera: one worker caste whose sizes run from about 5 to 18 mm, monophasic, Longhurst and Howse 1979; no soldiers, every worker raids and stings). Founding is colony_fission: a real queen never founds alone, a colony splits in two with a new queen (M9); until then a summoned queen starts an empty colony that spawn-egg workers near her join, or /antcolonies matabele <workers> makes one whole (the user's pick, 2026-10-24). So there is no founding section: a queen alone is never sealed in, digs nothing and lays nothing. nest.dug false: no planned nest is dug; the shallow nest (step 1d, MatabeleNest) is the best site within 32 blocks, a dead termite mound first, then under a fallen log, else the ground (a shaft and two rooms 3 and 5 down), and the workers dig only to open and join its spaces (the queen digs nothing); a room still holding dead comb is taken once it has rotted away. Hunger is on from the start (the user's pick, 2026-10-24): a colony whose prey pile (step 1e) runs empty goes hungry and starves; worker: slow after 2 days without a meal, dead after 4 (my picks, to confirm; real colonies raid termites 2 to 4 times a day and keep no store, so a colony cut off from termites dies fast); the queen dies after starve_ticks wanting food (5 days, my pick), but never while she is alone (a queen with no workers counts as founding). The brood numbers wait for the nest (1d). colony.max_workers 2500, the top of a real colony (400 to 2,500); real_cap and crew 50 as the termites. food: they eat only termites, from the prey pile (step 1e, the colony part prey_pile: stung, paralysed termites in the queen's room, a layer about 10 termites, rotten after a day and carried out to a heap beside the entrance; stocked by /antcolonies prey until the raids exist); the items tag is empty, no plants, the store's heap block an unused stand-in (they keep no store); worker.diet: young and old eat from the prey pile (nurse_food), one layer makes workers_per_piece 10 meals, one termite per ant a day (the user's pick, 2026-10-24), no mouth-to-mouth feeding (real Megaponera larvae are laid on the prey and eat it themselves, the queen eats from the pile); forage_at is empty: they stay in the nest (real Megaponera leave it only to raid, by day, step 4; my pick, 2026-10-24). refuse: a dead ant's body crumbles after corpse_decay_ticks (the dead are carried home in step 5).
_parts_note: prey_pile (M8 step 1e): the colony's food, termites in the queen's room, the nurses' food too. nest_defence (M8 step 2e): the colony stings a player who provokes it (the defence section). raids (M8 step 3): the scouts (3a, the raids.scouting section) and the raid columns (3b, the raids.column section).

worker_sizes._note: The real size spread of Megaponera workers (Longhurst and Howse 1979, from head widths: about half the workers majors, a quarter in between, a quarter minors; majors about 15 mm long, minors 9 to 11, the whole spread 5 to 18; the user's pick 'real count', 2026-10-24). Each new worker rolls its length from groups (share, the shortest, the commonest, the longest; a triangle between them), keeps it for life (saved) and is drawn at that length: with the major's model (made for major_model_mm) or the minor's (minor_model_mm), whichever its length is nearer (by ratio), scaled from it. The minor model is half the major's (2:1), so a real 10 mm minor is drawn a third bigger than the minor model.

worker._rest_in_rooms_note: With nothing to do the workers go down into the nest's rooms and stay there, never in the shaft (real Megaponera crowd into their chamber with the queen and the brood; the user's report 2026-10-24: they piled up at the top of the chimney).

body_language._note: Personality ranges all open (as before 1c, when the ant read the termites' numbers); no naps, hot ground or noticing yet.

fight._note: M8 step 2a, the shared fight system (fight.FightNumbers). Health and damage per body, my picks, to confirm in the user's first fight test (the numbers the bodies had in code before): a major 10 health (two to four soldier bites; real majors seldom die in a raid, minors more often), a minor 5, the queen 20. Damage only counts on what it does not hunt (a chicken; the player comes in step 2e): on termites, its prey, every blow is a paralysing sting that pricks for half a point and never kills (fight.Fights). prey: Macrotermes, the termites it lives on.
fight._legs_note: M8 step 2d: majors and minors can have legs bitten off by termite soldiers (the chance is the soldier's leg_cut in macrotermes.json); the queen keeps hers until 2e gives her a fight.
fight._look_over_note: M8 fight polish, round A: after felling a termite the ant stands over it, its antennae on it, this long (the shortest and longest, ticks: 1 to 2 s, my pick, to confirm), then turns to the next; one termite at a time, each blow played to its end (real raids: the attack at a feeding site lasts 5 to 30 minutes, Yusuf 2026).
fight._give_up_note: M8 fight polish, round B: with no termite in reach the ant searches round the feeding spot, antennae down, this long (ticks: 2 minutes, my pick, to confirm) before its fight is over (real raids: the attack lasts 5 to 30 minutes, the ants searching the opened galleries and the ground, Yusuf 2026).
fight._clamped_note: M8 step 2c, a termite soldier clamped on a leg (the user's calls 2026-10-25; Frank et al. 2017: the worst handicap measured, the ant crawling home; nestmates took the termites off in 9 cases in 10, the leg kept): slowing, a living soldier on the leg slows it this share (75 percent), it fights no more and goes home; head_slowing, a dead head left locked on slows it 10 percent and it may fight again; care_ticks, a nestmate in the nest works this long (30 s) to take it off; clean, the chance the leg is kept (9 in 10, else the leg comes off with it). slowing, head_slowing and care_ticks are my picks, to confirm.

scouting._note: M8 step 3a, the scouts (colony.Raids, MatabeleScoutGoal). Real Megaponera (Longhurst and Howse 1979, Yusuf 2026): lone scouts search for termites feeding under cover, look the place over and run home laying a scent line, which the raid column follows. scout_hours: the hours scouts search, in clock hours, all day 6 to 19:30 (the user's pick 2026-11-03, so a colony finds termites sooner; night scouting in the hot season waits for the shared season source), never in the rain. hours: the raid hours, mornings 6 to 11 and evenings 16 to 19 (the paper says 16 to 19:30; raid rework R7: no raid leaves after 19:00 and one still out at 19:30, raids.hours_and_sound.dusk, turns home): a raid only leaves then, so a find made between them waits for the next raid hours (no new scouts meanwhile). A colony whose prey pile holds less than a day's food sends one scout per workers_per_scout workers (at least 1, at most most_scouts; 1 per 50 up to 5, the user's pick 2026-11-03), majors only. A scout rechecks the colony's good spots first, then searches one piece of the land round the nest: a slice of slice_degrees of one ring, in arcs arc_step apart. Raid rework R5: the first ring is first_range deep, the next ones range_step each; trips search the nearest ring with a piece not searched lately first (near to far); a piece counts as searched only when a scout comes home empty from most of it, and only once every piece within the search range came home empty does the range grow by a ring, up to most_range (the real foraging range, about 95 m; a block counts as a metre for distances); it shrinks back after finds (raids.choosing). It smells termites within smell blocks (out of their mound, never in it, or in their dug feeding galleries and runways), looks a find over inspect_ticks, and goes home; nothing by trip_ticks: home empty. A slice searched empty is searched again after slice_fade_ticks; a good spot is forgotten after spot_fade_ticks unchecked or spot_misses empty checks. Every number my pick, to confirm.
scouting._hours_note: Raid rework R7 (the user's answer, 2026-11-04): no raid leaves after 19:00, so the evening raid hours end there (the paper's 19:30 is now raids.hours_and_sound.dusk, when a raid still out turns home).

choosing._note: Raid rework R5, scouts that choose (colony.Raids, MatabeleScoutGoal). Real Megaponera (Frank and Linsenmair 2017, Animal Behaviour, optimal foraging in the group-hunting termite specialist): rich termite sites are raided over the whole foraging range, poor ones only near the nest, and the raid's size follows the termites the scout found; a hungry colony sends more scouts and bigger raids. A scout smells only real feeding: termites out of their mound, or a feeding gallery or runway fed at by day (termites eating there out of sight, counted as by_day_termites termites); a bare gallery cell is no find. It walks up to inspect_from blocks of the find (just outside the termites' 3-block feel) and counts the termites within its smell all through its look (inspect_ticks near it), keeping the most at once; a find's worth is 3 a termite. A find is taken only if its worth reaches (least_worth + worth_per_block for each block from the nest) times a hunger factor, from hungry_ease for a starving colony to 1 for a nearly fed one; else the scout passes it over and searches on. A nearly fed colony sends fed_scouts of its scouts (rounded up), a starving one all of them. The search range shrinks one ring every shrink_ticks (a game day) after a find, back toward the ring of the colony's latest finds. Real numbers, noted only (Frank and Linsenmair 2017, Yusuf 2026): a real colony has about 10 to 20 scouts, searching in two sessions a day, a session sometimes over an hour; the user's 1 scout per 50 workers up to 5, searching all day, are kept. Every number my pick, to confirm.

mound_clue._note: Raid rework R6, the mound as a clue (the user's idea, 2026-11-03; colony.Raids, MatabeleScoutGoal). Not described in the papers; believable, as Macrotermes feed in galleries spreading out from their mound, the feeding spots 10 to 30 blocks past its foot. A scout searching that comes within notice blocks of a living termite mound's foot (a mound the colony has not ringed lately and no other scout is ringing) searches round it in widening rings ring_step apart, the first ring_step / 2 past the foot, out to past_foot blocks past it (its smell covers the gaps); its trip is extra_ticks longer, once a trip; points past the colony's most_range are left out. A mound ringed with nothing found is left fade_ticks. A tunnel of termites going to food (a gallery out to a feeding place, or the way to a mud runway) smelt within smell blocks on the way, wherever the scout is, is followed outward, away from the mound, to its end, a point every follow_every blocks along it; what it finds there must still pass the choosing rules. Every number my pick, to confirm.

hours_and_sound._note: Raid rework R7, hours and sound (colony.Raids, colony.RaidColumn). Raids end by dusk (the user's answer, 2026-11-04): no raid leaves after 19:00 (the evening raid hours in scouting.hours end there: time to reach a spot and come home), a raid still out at dusk (19:30) stops where it is, picks up what it stung and walks home, and until the morning's first raid hour (6:00) it stays dusk, so a find made after 19:00 waits for the morning. Rare night raids in the hot season (Yusuf 2026) wait for the shared season source (Serene Seasons, M9). A raid a command sends outside the raid hours (/antcolonies raid, /antcolonies scout anytime) keeps no hours. The attack: once no termite has been about the spot (within carry.collect_reach) for quiet_ticks, the attack is over (real raids: the attack at the feeding site lasts about 10 to 20 minutes, the termites stung, fled or sealed in; Yusuf 2026; column.fight_ticks is the most it may last). The squeak (Hoelldobler et al. 1994: the columns' stridulation is no message between the ants but a warning to big animals): the raider nearest a player within squeak_hear blocks squeaks, squeak_quiet loud every squeak_every_far ticks at that distance, up to squeak_loud every squeak_every_near ticks at squeak_loud_at blocks, before anyone stings. A column marching into land not ticking within edge_look blocks ahead of its front turns home at that edge (until drawn-only ants, M8 step 4). Every number my pick, to confirm.

column._note: M8 step 3b, the raid column (colony.RaidColumn, MatabeleRaidGoal). Real Megaponera (Longhurst and Howse 1979, Hoelldobler et al. 1994, Frank et al. 2017-2018, Yusuf 2026): the scout home from a find recruits nestmates at the entrance and leads them out along its scent line; the raid's size follows what the scout found (Frank 2018), 30 to 75 percent of the colony (Yusuf 2026). ants_per_worth ants for each point of the find's worth (a feeding gallery cell 1, a termite 3), at least least_raid, at most least_share (a fed colony) to most_share (a starving one) of the workers; at most most_real walk as real ants, the rest are numbers till step 4. The recruits mill round the entrance least_form_ticks to form_ticks (those not out by then stay home). The march: spacing blocks between ants, single file for the first single_file blocks, then up to abreast side by side; the scout at the front waits while the ants keeping up are strung out more than stretch blocks behind (the column moves in surges). It stops stop_short blocks before the find and bunches up (at most gather_ticks), then every ant attacks at once (majors break the mud open, minors go in; the termite workers first, soldiers only in the way), at most fight_ticks; then they regroup there (at most regroup_ticks) and walk home along the trail as a column, every ant home or let go after home_ticks. Every number my pick, to confirm.
column._fight_ticks_note: Raid rework R7: the attack's longest, 2 minutes (was 5; the raid diary's attacks ran about 4 minutes, a raid out from 8:00 to 14:00 in game hours). Most attacks now end sooner, quiet_ticks after the last termite about (raids.hours_and_sound). My pick, to confirm.

carry._note: M8 step 3c, home with the prey (colony.RaidColumn, BringPreyGoal). Real Megaponera (Longhurst and Howse 1979, Yusuf 2026): after the fight the raiders gather the stung termites, a major holding a bundle of up to about 12 under its jaws, a minor 1 to 3, and walk home as a column; the prey is eaten in the nest. A worker holds least_major (the shortest drawn as a major) to most_major (the longest major), least_minor to most_minor for a minor, by its length. The raiders pick up the paralysed termites within collect_reach blocks of the find, workers before soldiers, at most collect_ticks, each pick-up pick_ticks. A raid that found nothing spreads round the spot up to spread_reach blocks for spread_ticks, a raider seeing a termite within spread_see blocks going for it, then gathers what it stung; still nothing: home, and the find counts an empty check. Laden, the column walks home at laden_pace of its pace. At home each carrier lays its termites on the prey pile, termites_per_layer to a layer (one that finds no way to the pile in bring_ticks has them laid there out of sight). A raider that leaves the column hurt (crippled, or a soldier clamped on a leg) follows the raid's trail home alone, at most limp_ticks. Every number my pick, to confirm, but the loads (real).

trails._note: M8 raid rework R4, the scent trails (colony.ScentTrails). Real Megaponera lay their trail from the poison gland, every raider on the way out (so the way home does not hang on the scout), and it lasts up to about 29 hours (Hoelldobler et al. 1994; a game day counted as a real day, so 29,000 ticks). A trail a raid column walked lasts lasting_ticks after it was last walked; a lone scout's line, weaker, scout_lasting_ticks; a later raid to the same spot follows a trail still smelt, and with the trail gone and the scout dead nobody knows the way. A trail is broken where a block is dug or put on it or water covers it: the column stops at the gap and the front ants cast about at least cast_ticks, plus cast_per_block for each block of the gap; a far side within cast_reach blocks is picked up and the gap mended with new scent; a wider gap, after cast_give_ticks, is crossed only if a former scout walks in the column (it leads on from memory, a hypothesis in AntWiki, never tested), else the raid turns home (the way home is always found). Every number my pick, to confirm, but the 29 hours.

defence._note: M8 step 2e, the player (the user's calls, 2026-10-25; fight.NestDefence, fight.DefenceNumbers). Real Megaponera sting anyone who breaks into the nest or treads on a raid column, a sting among the most painful of any ant, and squeak loudly as they do. A player provokes the colony by breaking its nest (a block within nest_radius of the entrance or of a room), hitting a member, standing in a column (touching a fighting ant column_touch_ticks, 1 s) or staying on the nest (look: walking within radius of the entrance brings ants out to look, who sting if the player stays sting_after ticks, 3 s, then go in after lasts). The ants within scent_reach of the trouble come at once; trouble at the nest brings defenders out in waves: first_wave, the nearest the entrance, then wave more every wave_every ticks while it goes on, at most most out; each provocation keeps it going keep_going ticks (30 s); they give up past reach blocks from the trouble (16). The queen stings only in her room (queen_reach 3). sting: 2 hearts (damage 4, before armour), at most once every every_ticks from one ant; the pain (slowed, the screen's edge red) pain_ticks, more_ticks longer for each sting in the last window_ticks, at most most_ticks. A player in creative or spectator mode never provokes them. Every number my pick, to confirm.
